# HStackedBarChart

> Normalized percentage columns for changing multi-series data, built from HTML spans.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This describes repository source for version 0.9.0. Match documentation to your installed source/release.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HStackedBarChart` from `@hearth-ui/vue`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-stacked-bar-chart>`.
- Constructor: `HearthStackedBarChartElement` from `@hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Diagrams.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HStackedBarChart.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- Each column independently normalizes nonnegative finite values to 100%; all-zero columns stay empty. Up to eight series, identified by stable ids. The application supplies time-ordered columns and owns live updates. Heights transition under normal motion; reduced motion is immediate. Keyboard inspection, legend labels and an exact-value/percentage data table convey meaning beyond color. The latest maxPoints columns are shown (default 60, maximum 240).

## Public API

columns: ChartColumn[] · series: ChartSeries[] · label, description, unit, selected: string · height, maxPoints: number

A `?` marks optional source props. Props with defaults may be omitted. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    columns: ChartColumn[];
    series: ChartSeries[];
    label: string;
    description?: string;
    unit?: string;
    selected?: string;
    height?: number;
    maxPoints?: number;
};
```

### Defaults

```ts
{ columns: () => [], series: () => [] }
```

### Events

select(string)

```ts
type Emits = {
    select: [
        id: string
    ];
};
```

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose argument arrays in `event.detail`. Listen on the element. Native events such as `click` retain their normal payloads. The elements package provides framework-independent DOM event types.

### Slots

None

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Web components do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

base, title, viewport, column, segment, tooltip, legend, data, empty

Use `hearth-stacked-bar-chart::part(part-name)` for an exposed part or inherited `--h-*` tokens for shared styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Supporting types

```ts
export interface ChartColumn {
    id: string;
    label: string;
    values: Record<string, number>;
}

export interface ChartSeries {
    id: string;
    label: string;
    tone?: Tone;
}

export type Tone = "neutral" | "accent" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "info";
```

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { HStackedBarChart } from '@hearth-ui/vue';
import '@hearth-ui/vue/styles.css';

</script>

<template>
  <HStackedBarChart label="Request outcomes" :series="[{id:'ok',label:'Success'},{id:'retry',label:'Retry'}]" :columns="[{id:'a',label:'09:00',values:{ok:80,retry:20}},{id:'b',label:'10:00',values:{ok:95,retry:5}}]" />
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point. For field submission, use an owning native form; the auth page already contains its own form.

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

This is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Initial array/object properties are assigned before connection to establish reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@hearth-ui/elements';
import '@hearth-ui/elements/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-stacked-bar-chart');
Object.assign(element, {
  "label": "Request outcomes",
  "series": [
    {
      "id": "ok",
      "label": "Success",
      "tone": "success"
    },
    {
      "id": "retry",
      "label": "Retry",
      "tone": "warning"
    },
    {
      "id": "error",
      "label": "Error",
      "tone": "danger"
    }
  ],
  "columns": [
    {
      "id": "a",
      "label": "09:00",
      "values": {
        "ok": 80,
        "retry": 15,
        "error": 5
      }
    },
    {
      "id": "b",
      "label": "10:00",
      "values": {
        "ok": 65,
        "retry": 25,
        "error": 10
      }
    },
    {
      "id": "c",
      "label": "11:00",
      "values": {
        "ok": 92,
        "retry": 6,
        "error": 2
      }
    }
  ]
});

element.addEventListener('select', event => {
  const [value] = event.detail;
  // Update your application state using value.
});

mount.append(element);
```
